holidays.name: National Senior Citizens Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the wisdom, stories, and sass of older adults, with grandparents everywhere getting extra hugs, phone calls, and probably some unsolicited advice about wearing a sweater.
holidays.origin: Proclaimed in 1988 by President Ronald Reagan, who signed Proclamation 5847 and was himself 77 at the time. Congress had passed a joint resolution to recognize the day.
holidays.funFact: Reagan was the oldest sitting U.S. president at the time, and he was re-elected at age 73, which made the proclamation a bit of a personal victory lap.

holidays.name: National Spumoni Day
holidays.description: A salute to the layered Italian frozen dessert packed with cherries, pistachios, and chocolate, which is basically ice cream wearing a fancy tuxedo.
holidays.origin: Spumoni traces back to Naples, Italy, and was brought to America by Italian immigrants. The exact origin of the commemorative day is unclear, but it has become a popular food-calendar fixture for dessert fans.
holidays.funFact: The word 'spumone' comes from the Italian 'spuma,' meaning foam, a nod to its light, airy texture.

holidays.name: World Honey Bee Day (Third Saturday of August)
holidays.description: A buzzworthy day dedicated to appreciating honey bees, who work tirelessly pollinating our crops and who never once ask for a vacation day. Fans celebrate by planting flowers, buying local honey, and building bee-friendly habitats.
holidays.origin: Started by beekeepers and bee advocates in the United States in 2009 as National Honey Bee Day to raise awareness of pollinator decline, and later expanded to a worldwide observance.
holidays.funFact: A single honey bee produces only about one-twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in its entire lifetime.

holidays.name: National Poet's Day (Observed in Some Calendars)
holidays.description: A day for rhyme lovers, haiku hoarders, and anyone who has ever scribbled a verse on a napkin. Celebrate by writing a limerick about your lunch or reading poetry out loud to unsuspecting coworkers.
holidays.origin: Poetry observances have long been scattered through the year, and this unofficial date has been embraced by poetry fans on social media and in community writing groups.
holidays.funFact: The oldest known named poet in history is Enheduanna, a Mesopotamian priestess who lived around 2300 BCE.

holidays.name: International Day of Remembrance and Tribute to the Victims of Terrorism
holidays.description: A solemn but important observance honoring survivors and victims of terrorism and promoting the importance of support, dignity, and justice for those affected.
holidays.origin: Established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2017, with August 21 chosen to give a day of voice and recognition to victims worldwide.
holidays.funFact: It is one of the few UN-recognized days dedicated specifically to listening to the stories of survivors and victims' families.
